questions.question: Why did my AI agent bill jump from $80 to $400 overnight?
questions.answer_summary: A common cause is the agent entering a loop and calling the same tool dozens of times (one developer traced it to 47 repeated calls) before anyone notices; without cost caps or circuit breakers the spend keeps compounding.

questions.question: Why do agentic workflows cost so much more than a regular chatbot query?
questions.answer_summary: Agentic workflows consume roughly 5-30x more tokens per task than a standard chatbot query because they re-read context repeatedly across multi-step tool calls; re-sent context alone accounts for a majority of total inference bills.

questions.question: What is 'context rot' and how does it affect agent costs?
questions.answer_summary: Accuracy degrades for most tested models as input length grows, especially in the middle of long contexts after 20-30 turns, forcing more retries and re-processing which drives cost up further.

questions.question: How much can prompt caching actually save on agent costs?
questions.answer_summary: Prompt caching can cut costs roughly 90% on cached tokens (e.g., $0.30 vs $3.00 per million tokens on Claude), with break-even typically reached after about 2.3 cache reuses within an hour-long window.

questions.question: What's a realistic monthly cost range for running an AI agent in production?
questions.answer_summary: Estimates found ranged from about $200/month for a lightweight coding assistant to $5,000+/month for a high-volume customer support agent, with mid-size custom agents commonly landing between $1,000-$5,000/month including infrastructure.

questions.question: Why did a company's inference bill jump from $12,000 to $68,000 in six weeks?
questions.answer_summary: A healthcare company's costs spiked due to retrieval faults in its RAG pipeline causing repeated/uncontrolled retries, tripling token cost per operation in some cases.

questions.question: Is inference the biggest cost of running an AI agent?
questions.answer_summary: No - inference is estimated at only about 20% of total cost of ownership; the remaining roughly 80% comes from orchestration, monitoring, and governance infrastructure.

questions.question: Why do idle AI agents still cost money even when no one is using them?
questions.answer_summary: Agent usage is bursty (heavy use for minutes, then long idle periods) but servers often run 24/7, meaning up to 90% of backend cost under traditional always-on deployment can go to idle time.

questions.question: What basic safeguards should be in place before putting an agent into production to control cost?
questions.answer_summary: Practitioners on Hacker News list token estimation, state persistence, cost monitoring and rate limiting, circuit breakers, retry logic, context caching, and deadlock detection as baseline requirements before shipping.

questions.question: How fast can enterprise AI agent spend grow at a large company?
questions.answer_summary: At Uber, Claude Code adoption went from 32% to 84% of a 5,000-engineer org between December and March, with per-engineer monthly costs of $500-$2,000, exhausting the annual AI budget by April.

questions.question: How much of AI agent cost is actually recoverable through optimization?
questions.answer_summary: Estimates suggest 60-85% of agent inference spend is recoverable through a combination of prompt caching, intelligent model routing, and hard budget enforcement.

questions.question: How much is total industry spend on AI agent/model API costs growing?
questions.answer_summary: Model API spend roughly doubled from about $3.5B to $8.4B between late 2024 and mid-2025 across the industry, reflecting how fast agent-related inference spend is scaling.
